title: Regional reservoir affinity router with degraded-path shedding
creator: Maya Chen
description: Implement a 'regional reservoir' routing layer that combines soft geo-affinity with capacity-aware reservoirs per region, latency SLO adherence, and graceful degraded-path shedding. Goal: keep p95 <= 180ms for interactive endpoints while reducing cross-region failovers and minimizing cold-model evictions. This ticket covers design, prototype, canary rollout, and dashboarding for the feature.
acceptance_criteria: Runtime exposes per-region reservoir occupancy metric and API for reservation/charge/debit operations
Router uses reservoir occupancy + p95 latency signal to calculate region weights and route decisions
When occupancy > threshold or latency breaches SLO, router triggers regional circuit-breaker and enables degraded-paths (lighter model variants or token-shedding) before redirecting to remote region
End-to-end latency p95 for production traffic serving small chat requests remains <= 180ms in normal conditions and <= 400ms under controlled overload with degraded-paths enabled
Grafana dashboard with reservoir occupancy, regional circuit-breaker state, hedging events, and per-model QPS is available
Canary rollout plan executed in us-west and eu-west with automatic rollback on error-rate > 0.5% above baseline
tasks: Design: define reservoir model (tokens vs credit), decay rates, and eviction hints
Design: specify circuit-breaker state machine and transition thresholds for latency and occupancy
Implement: reservoir counters in routing service with Redis-backed fallback and local cache
Implement: weight calculation combining geo-affinity, latency score, and occupancy penalty
Integrate: degraded-path selection that swaps to quantized model variant or token-shed policy
Test: unit tests for weight math, circuit-breaker transitions, and degraded-path selection
Benchmark: synthetic load tests across 3 regions using k6 to validate p50/p95/p99 behaviors
Observability: add Grafana panels, alerts, and tracing tags for hedged/redirected requests
Rollout: staged canary in us-west (5%), eu-west (2%), monitor 48h, increase to 25% then 100% if healthy
design_notes: Reservoir model: use a replenishing token bucket per region where tokens represent 'serveable units' adjusted by model size and gpu-sharing factor
Occupancy penalty: weight = base_affinity * exp(-alpha * (tokens_available / tokens_capacity)) * latency_penalty
Latency score sources: service p95 windowed over 1m and 5m, fallback to synthetic probe when traffic sparse
Circuit-breaker triggers: open when p95 > 250ms OR tokens_available < 10% for two consecutive 30s windows
Degraded-path order: (1) quantized model variant, (2) shorter max_tokens, (3) token-shedding policy, (4) route to remote region
Soft geo-affinity: prefer local region while occupancy and latency metrics are healthy; affinity is percentage-based to allow gradual draining
Fallback storage: local in-memory counters for fast path with Redis as eventual source-of-truth to avoid global contention
Cost consideration: prefer local degraded-paths (quantized models) before cross-region routing to avoid egress and higher latency
tradeoffs: Using local in-memory counters improves latency but risks temporary divergence across replicas; we mitigate with eventual reconciliation and conservative thresholds
Reservoir token model simplifies accounting but requires careful tuning to avoid oscillations during bursty traffic
Favoring degraded-paths reduces user-perceived availability of full model fidelity; must be paired with visibility so downstream teams understand quality mode
Probing frequency affects responsiveness to failures but increases probing load; choose adaptive probing based on traffic volume
implementation_notes: Added new thrift endpoints for ReserveTokens/ReleaseTokens with idempotency keys
Redis schema: HASH region:{region_id}:reservoir with fields capacity, tokens, last_refill_ts
Default capacity heuristics derived from recent 1h GPU utilization and model qps profile
Degraded-path flags emitted as trace tags: degraded_mode=quantized|shortened|shed_tokens
Added feature flag 'regional_reservoir_v1' for controlled rollout
testing_summary: Unit tests: coverage for token accounting, weight math, and state transitions (CI: pass)
Staging load tests: 10k rps synthetic chat traffic across us-west/eu-west/ap-south, observed expected shed rates and no silent failures
Canary baseline: first 48h in us-west showed p95 within 170-185ms; triggered two short degraded-path episodes during GPU drain window
Failure injection: simulated eu-west GPU OOM; router opened eu-west circuit-breaker and used quantized variant in-region before failing over to us-west
Regression tests: integration with rolling upgrades to ensure reservoir reconciliation after process restarts
metrics_and_dashboards: grafana/dashboard/RegionalReservoirOverview (panels: tokens_available, tokens_capacity, occupancy_pct, regional_p95, hedged_requests, degraded_mode_rate)
alerts: RRV-HighOccupancy (occupancy > 90% for 2m), RRV-RegionalLatency (p95 > 250ms for 1m), RRV-FallthroughRate (remote-routing > 5% for 5m)
traces: sampled traces include field routed_region, chosen_mode, reservoir_state, circuit_state
canary_plan: Phase 1: enable feature flag for internal service-to-service calls in us-west (5%) for 48h
Phase 2: expand to 25% in us-west and 2% eu-west, monitor capacity and error-rate for 72h
Phase 3: enable degraded-paths globally for services with experimental opt-in, continue incremental ramp to 100%
Rollback criteria: sustained increase in 5xxs by >0.5% or p95 increase > 20% sustained for 15m
